data.note:
Reflection: Compound was mitomycin C, confirmed as DNA inhibitor by ChEMBL (CHEMBL105, PubChem CID 5746) and annotated as DNA damage. I concluded Aurora kinase inhibitors (0.65) based on consistent polyploidy phenotype: massive nuclear enlargement (nuc_area z=20-26), increased integrated DNA content (z=5-14), frac_large_nucleus z=8-9.5, and visual binucleate giant cells at 1-3 uM, plus NSC vote 2/4 Aurora and 8/10 neighbors Aurora. This mimics Aurora failure of cytokinesis.

In hindsight DNA crosslink-induced G2 arrest also produces enlarged nuclei/high DNA content with reduced proliferation (cell_count z -3 to -5.6) without microtubule loss (preserved tubulin at 1uM). The split NSC vote (Aurora 2, DNA damage 1, Protein synthesis 1) should have raised uncertainty; the 10uM high-dose well with tub_std/contrast z>14 was a toxic/spreading artefact favouring microtubule stabilizer description but not representative.

Literature confirms mitomycin C is a DNA interstrand crosslinker causing DNA damage: preferential binding to mitomycin C-DNA interstrand crosslink (PMID 17512921) and mitomycin C-induced DNA double-strand breaks (PMID 41199376). Next time I would weight DNA-damage G2 polyploidy equally when binucleation is rare and prioritize intermediate-dose replicates rather than a toxic 10uM dose.

Next lab experiment: gamma-H2AX / phospho-p53 vs phospho-Aurora/p-H3S10 immunofluorescence plus cell-cycle analysis to distinguish DNA-damage G2 arrest from Aurora cytokinesis failure, with reference DNA-damaging and Aurora inhibitor class controls.

reflection.text:
Unblinded compound: mitomycin C (PubChem CID 5746, ChEMBL CHEMBL105, mechanism DNA inhibitor, target DNA CHEMBL2311221 - name and BBBC021 structure agree). Verdict: incorrect. Truth MOA = DNA damage, agent/scientist MOA = Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.65, protocol 1-NN majority vote 2/4 wells Aurora, summed similarity 1.036). Review approved on exhausted budget grounds.

What the evidence got right: The core phenotype was correctly identified as massive nuclear enlargement/polyploidy. e2 (0.1 uM, rep1, 595 cells) nuc_area z=+20.5, nuc_major_axis +10.9; e7 (1 uM) nuc_area +26.4, major_axis +15.4, frac_large_nucleus +9.5; e8 (3 uM, 399 cells) nuc_area +26.7, major_axis +15.3, nuc_dna_integrated +14.0. This was visible as large nuclei/binucleation noted by microscopist in e13 (density similar, 10 observations, candidates: Aurora) and e14 (density lower, 7 observations, candidates: Aurora, DNA damage). Dose_response e10 and e11 correctly showed saturation (rho -0.20 p=0.8 for both nuc_area and nuc_dna_integrated across 0.1-10 uM) - we were already at ceiling at the lowest acquired dose. DNA damage was retained as runner-up hypothesis at p=0.20 in e15 with supporting e11,e14, and k-neighbour DNA damage 1/10 in e6 and 2/10 in e9 was never zero. Literature in this run supports truth: PMID 41199376 Mitomycin C-induced DNA double-strand breaks, PMID 17512921 mitomycin C-DNA interstrand crosslink, PMID 19791750 reductive activation of mitomycin C, consistent with ChEMBL DNA inhibitor annotation.

What misled us and why:

1. Phenotypic overlap between Aurora inhibition and DNA damage-induced G2 arrest/polyploidy. Aurora-like polyploidy with intact morphology dominated microscopy (e13) and the atlas. e9 NSC vote over 4 wells was 2/4 Aurora, k-neighbour 8/10 Aurora vs 2/10 DNA damage, which we treated as decisive in e15/e16. The protocol per-well details show why this was fragile: w_9da6828375 at 1 uM was actually nearest DNA damage with the highest single-well similarity in the run (0.642), versus Aurora wells at 0.484 (0.1 uM) and 0.553 (3 uM). Majority vote discarded the strength of the DNA damage hit. Summed similarity Aurora 1.036 vs DNA damage 0.642 reflects two weak Aurora hits outvoting one strong DNA damage hit.

2. Acquisition choice - no low-dose titration. We acquired e2 at 0.1 uM already showing z=+20.5 and e7/e8 showing +26.4/+26.7, so e10/e11 flat dose-response was saturation, not lack of effect. e1 shows 8 doses 0.003-10 uM were available. We never sampled 0.003-0.03 uM where DNA damage dose-dependence and lack of acute cytokinesis failure might have separated Aurora (sharp binucleation threshold) from DNA crosslinker G2 accumulation. With 0 wells left, we could not correct.

3. High-dose cytoskeletal noise. e3 at 10 uM (155 cells, strong depletion vs 595-637 cells at lower doses) showed tub_glcm_contrast +25.1, act_glcm_contrast +14.5, tub_std +14.2 with perfect tubulin dose dependence e12 rho=+1.00 p=0, and microscopist e5 calling Microtubule stabilizers. This created a Protein synthesis NSC vote at 10 uM (per-well table: w_b962c28c9c nearest Protein synthesis 0.568) and e6 initial vote 1/2 Protein synthesis, 5/10 k-neighbours Protein synthesis. We correctly downweighted this to 0.05 in e15 by invoking e13/e9, but it consumed budget and added atlas noise, and reflected toxicity secondary to DNA damage rather than primary MOA.

4. We over-weighted atlas k-neighbour counts and microscopist Aurora calls (e13,e14) relative to the microscopist's own DNA damage inclusion in e14 and the quantitative DNA integrated signal in e8. No discriminating assay (e.g., phospho-Histone H3 Ser10, phospho-Aurora, gamma-H2AX) is available in this Cell Painting run to break the Aurora vs DNA damage polyploidy degeneracy.

Lesson: For DNA crosslinkers like mitomycin C, massive nuc_area and nuc_dna_integrated with frac_large_nucleus can mimic Aurora cytokinesis failure in morphology-only space. When saturation is reached at the lowest sampled dose (e10/e11 rho -0.20), and per-well similarities show a competing DNA damage hit with higher similarity despite minority vote, the correct move is to sample lower doses and require a second modality rather than accepting 2/4 majority at 8/10 neighbours.
what_was_right: Polyploidy/large-nucleus phenotype captured by extreme z-scores in e2,e7,e8 and microscopist e13/e14
K-neighbour DNA damage signal present e6 1/10 e9 2/10 and per-well DNA damage hit at 1uM 0.642 not ignored
High-dose microtubule/protein synthesis noise correctly downweighted
what_was_wrong: Treated 2/4 Aurora majority and 8/10 neighbours as decisive despite stronger single DNA damage similarity
Flat nuc_area/DNA integrated dose response interpreted as Aurora-consistent rather than saturated DNA damage
No low-dose acquisition to resolve dose-dependence below 0.1uM

Unblinded compound: mitomycin C (PubChem CID 5746, ChEMBL CHEMBL105, mechanism DNA inhibitor, target DNA CHEMBL2311221 - name and BBBC021 structure agree). Verdict: incorrect. Truth MOA = DNA damage, agent/scientist MOA = Aurora kinase inhibitors (p=0.65, protocol 1-NN majority vote 2/4 wells Aurora, summed similarity 1.036). Review approved on exhausted budget grounds.

What the evidence got right: The core phenotype was correctly identified as massive nuclear enlargement/polyploidy. e2 (0.1 uM, rep1, 595 cells) nuc_area z=+20.5, nuc_major_axis +10.9; e7 (1 uM) nuc_area +26.4, major_axis +15.4, frac_large_nucleus +9.5; e8 (3 uM, 399 cells) nuc_area +26.7, major_axis +15.3, nuc_dna_integrated +14.0. This was visible as large nuclei/binucleation noted by microscopist in e13 (density similar, 10 observations, candidates: Aurora) and e14 (density lower, 7 observations, candidates: Aurora, DNA damage). Dose_response e10 and e11 correctly showed saturation (rho -0.20 p=0.8 for both nuc_area and nuc_dna_integrated across 0.1-10 uM) - we were already at ceiling at the lowest acquired dose. DNA damage was retained as runner-up hypothesis at p=0.20 in e15 with supporting e11,e14, and k-neighbour DNA damage 1/10 in e6 and 2/10 in e9 was never zero. Literature in this run supports truth: PMID 41199376 Mitomycin C-induced DNA double-strand breaks, PMID 17512921 mitomycin C-DNA interstrand crosslink, PMID 19791750 reductive activation of mitomycin C, consistent with ChEMBL DNA inhibitor annotation.

What misled us and why:

1. Phenotypic overlap between Aurora inhibition and DNA damage-induced G2 arrest/polyploidy. Aurora-like polyploidy with intact morphology dominated microscopy (e13) and the atlas. e9 NSC vote over 4 wells was 2/4 Aurora, k-neighbour 8/10 Aurora vs 2/10 DNA damage, which we treated as decisive in e15/e16. The protocol per-well details show why this was fragile: w_9da6828375 at 1 uM was actually nearest DNA damage with the highest single-well similarity in the run (0.642), versus Aurora wells at 0.484 (0.1 uM) and 0.553 (3 uM). Majority vote discarded the strength of the DNA damage hit. Summed similarity Aurora 1.036 vs DNA damage 0.642 reflects two weak Aurora hits outvoting one strong DNA damage hit.

2. Acquisition choice - no low-dose titration. We acquired e2 at 0.1 uM already showing z=+20.5 and e7/e8 showing +26.4/+26.7, so e10/e11 flat dose-response was saturation, not lack of effect. e1 shows 8 doses 0.003-10 uM were available. We never sampled 0.003-0.03 uM where DNA damage dose-dependence and lack of acute cytokinesis failure might have separated Aurora (sharp binucleation threshold) from DNA crosslinker G2 accumulation. With 0 wells left, we could not correct.

3. High-dose cytoskeletal noise. e3 at 10 uM (155 cells, strong depletion vs 595-637 cells at lower doses) showed tub_glcm_contrast +25.1, act_glcm_contrast +14.5, tub_std +14.2 with perfect tubulin dose dependence e12 rho=+1.00 p=0, and microscopist e5 calling Microtubule stabilizers. This created a Protein synthesis NSC vote at 10 uM (per-well table: w_b962c28c9c nearest Protein synthesis 0.568) and e6 initial vote 1/2 Protein synthesis, 5/10 k-neighbours Protein synthesis. We correctly downweighted this to 0.05 in e15 by invoking e13/e9, but it consumed budget and added atlas noise, and reflected toxicity secondary to DNA damage rather than primary MOA.

4. We over-weighted atlas k-neighbour counts and microscopist Aurora calls (e13,e14) relative to the microscopist's own DNA damage inclusion in e14 and the quantitative DNA integrated signal in e8. No discriminating assay (e.g., phospho-Histone H3 Ser10, phospho-Aurora, gamma-H2AX) is available in this Cell Painting run to break the Aurora vs DNA damage polyploidy degeneracy.

Lesson: For DNA crosslinkers like mitomycin C, massive nuc_area and nuc_dna_integrated with frac_large_nucleus can mimic Aurora cytokinesis failure in morphology-only space. When saturation is reached at the lowest sampled dose (e10/e11 rho -0.20), and per-well similarities show a competing DNA damage hit with higher similarity despite minority vote, the correct move is to sample lower doses and require a second modality rather than accepting 2/4 majority at 8/10 neighbours.

What was right:
- Polyploidy/large-nucleus phenotype captured by extreme z-scores in e2,e7,e8 and microscopist e13/e14
- K-neighbour DNA damage signal present e6 1/10 e9 2/10 and per-well DNA damage hit at 1uM 0.642 not ignored
- High-dose microtubule/protein synthesis noise correctly downweighted

What was wrong or missed:
- Treated 2/4 Aurora majority and 8/10 neighbours as decisive despite stronger single DNA damage similarity
- Flat nuc_area/DNA integrated dose response interpreted as Aurora-consistent rather than saturated DNA damage
- No low-dose acquisition to resolve dose-dependence below 0.1uM

Proposed next experiment: Not applicable - this is post-hoc reflection after unblinding; original next-experiment rationale was IF for phospho-Aurora/phospho-H3 to discriminate cytokinesis failure vs G2 arrest
